test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The population of a town increases at the rate of 10% every year. The present population is 1,000. In how many years will the population become 1,331?
solution:
**Given:**

Increase in population every year = 10%

Present population = 1000

Required population = 1331

**Concept Used:**

Compound Interest = Principal(1+(r)/(100))^t

**Calculation:**

⇒ Principal = 1000

⇒ Putting the values in the formula,

⇒ 1000(1+(10)/(100))^t=1331

⇒ ((100+10)/(100))^t=(1331)/(1000)

⇒ ((11)/(10))^t=(1331)/(1000)

⇒ ((11)/(10))^t=((11)/(10))³

⇒ Equating the values, we get t = 3 years.

**Therefore, the number of years in which population will become 1331 is 3 years.**
